why: Writing L1 as (1,-1,1)+t(2,3,4) and L2 as (3,k,0)+s(1,2,1), the x- and z-equations force t=-3/2, s=-5; the y-equation then gives k = -1+3t-2s = 9/2, and both lines meet at (-2,-11/2,-5). The coplanarity determinant is 2k-9, so k=9/2 is the unique value (option A, 2/9, is the reciprocal distractor).
10+120+252+120+10 = 512, i.e. the sum of the odd-index binomial coefficients of (1+x)^10 is 2^(10-1) = 2^9. Options B (1024) and C (1023) are distinct from it, so the match is unique.
(11000)_2 = 24 and (11)_2 = 3, so 24/3 = 8 exactly, which is 1000_2. The other options evaluate to 6, 7 and 10, all distinct.
Two planes are perpendicular exactly when their normals are orthogonal. Against n=(3,1,1) the four option normals give dot products 6, 2, 4 and 0, so only x-2y-z=6 qualifies.
The equation is 2x^2 + (1-k)x + 8 = 0; equal real roots need (1-k)^2 - 64 = 0, so 1-k = +/-8 and k = -7 or 9 (giving the repeated roots x = -2 and x = 2 respectively). Only option D lists that pair.
Inclusion-exclusion: 21+26+29-14-15-12+8 = 43. The Venn regions are all non-negative and consistent (8, 6, 7, 4 pairwise/triple and 3, 5, 10 exclusive), summing to 43, so the data is coherent.
(1+i)/(1-i) = i and (1-i)/(1+i) = -i, so the expression is i^4 + (-i)^4 = 1 + 1 = 2; sympy simplification confirms exactly 2.

Enumerating all 4! = 24 permutations, exactly one puts every letter in its own envelope, so the probability is 1/24. (Option B, 23/24, is the complement and option A, 11/12, matches nothing; P(no letter correct) is 3/8, also not offered.)
9 workers plus the owner is 10 people averaging 110, so the total is 1100; the 9 workers contribute 9 x 76 = 684, leaving 1100 - 684 = 416 for the owner.

dy/dx = 2x integrates to y = x^2 + C, and y(0)=0 gives C=0 (dsolve with that initial condition returns y = x^2). The other curves fail the slope condition away from the origin, e.g. option A has slope 3 at x=1/2 where 2x = 1.

why: C = 180 - 75 - 45 = 60. By the sine rule 2a-b = 2R(2 sin75 - sin45) = 2R(sqrt6/2) = sqrt6 R, while c = 2R sin60 = sqrt3 R, so 2a-b = sqrt2 c exactly (checked symbolically and at 50 digits). None of the other three options matches.

cos((x+T)^2) = cos(x^2) for all x would need 2Tx + T^2 constant mod 2pi in x, forcing T = 0; a 40-digit check rejects 2pi, sqrt(2pi) and pi as periods. The rival reading (cos x)^2 is ruled out by the options themselves: under it BOTH A (2pi) and D (pi) would be periods, so only the cos(x^2) reading yields a unique answer.

Subtracting a+(m-1)d = 1/n from a+(n-1)d = 1/m gives (m-n)d = (m-n)/(mn), so d = 1/(mn), and back-substitution gives a = 1/(mn) as well; hence a-d = 0 (verified symbolically and on the instance m=3, n=5).
100(a+99d) = 50(a+49d) gives 50a + 7450d = 0, so a = -149d and a_150 = a + 149d = 0. Option B is not an equivalent restatement: a_50 = -100d, so 150 x a_50 = -15000d, non-zero because d is non-zero.

The common terms of the two APs (d = 4 and d = 5) start at 11 and recur with difference lcm(4,5) = 20, i.e. 11, 31, 51, ...; the first 20 sum to (20/2)(22 + 19x20) = 4020, confirmed by intersecting the two generated sets.
